catalog_locator: §2.5.1 Stress, printed pp. 64-66 (PDF pages 64-66 of 223); affix stress classes §2.6.1, pp. 69-71; intonation §2.5.2, pp. 66-69.
catalog_quote: Phonetically, stress is signalled in Bakhtiari by the phonetic lengthening of vowels, increased loudness, and raised pitch. Stress is found on content words (verbs, nouns, adjectives and adverbs), where it is normally hosted by the last syllable of the stem, whatever the number of syllables in the word. 'hars ‘tear(drop)’ ... zah.'le ‘gall bladder’ ... ey.le.'ʋār ‘jaw’ ... Function words, however, are not stressed unless they are emphasized. ... Some affixes are inherently stressed, and others are unstressed (for a list of affixes, and their status with regard to stress, see 2.6.1). If a stressed affix is added to a stem, it takes the word stress; but if the affix is unstressed, stress stays on the stem. ... If there are two stressed suffixes, the second one carries the stress. ... If there is a stressed prefix as well as a stressed suffix, the stressed prefix takes the word stress. ...…

new_statements.rule_in_words: Persian-type stem-final stress: in content words stress falls on the last syllable of the stem regardless of length ('hars, zah.'le, ey.le.'vār). Affixes are lexically stressed or unstressed: a stressed suffix (definite -(e)ke, plural -gal, vocative -ay, verbal person endings) takes the stress, the last one winning if there are several, so the word is then final-stressed; unstressed suffixes and clitics (object -ne, pronominal clitics, copula -i) leave stress on the stem. Stressed prefixes (imperative be-, negative na-) override stressed suffixes. Function words are unstressed unless emphasized. Stress placement is contrastive in affix-class pairs (di'dom 'I saw' vs 'didom 'he/she saw me'; ton'di 'speed' vs 'tondi 'you are fast'). An alternative provisional coding would be morphological (stem-final default + affix stress classes).
new_statements.exceptions: Function words (vo 'and', men 'in', ayar 'if') unstressed unless emphasized; unstressed affixes/clitics keep stress on the stem; stressed prefixes be-/na- take stress away from stressed suffixes; minimal pairs by affix stress class. Phonetic cues: vowel lengthening, loudness, raised pitch; intonation (§2.5.2) raises pitch on stressed syllables of pragmatically salient words.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level stress on morphologically complex words (stem + affixes; clitics attach to a stress-bearing host, §2.4). Data are the Haft Lang Bakhtiari of co-author Ashraf Asadi from the area around Masjed Soleymān, Khuzestān (p. 13-14 of the book). Section 2.5.2 treats sentence intonation separately.
new_statements.identity_note: Anonby & Asadi 2014 describe the Haft Lang Bakhtiari of Masjed Soleymān (Khuzestān), the co-author's own variety; Bakhtiari has three large dialect areas (Masjed Soleymān, Shahr-e Kord/Chahar Mahal, Lorestan side) and the 2025 Bavadi article notes vowel-inventory variation across them, but no source examined suggests the stress rule differs. Glottocode bakh1245 covers all.
